scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user is asking if they're being an asshole (AITA) for lying to their boyfriend about his ex-girlfriend. Let me break this down step by step.

First, the scenario: The user is a college senior who started dating a guy four months ago. The guy had been dating another girl for two years, and they broke up because he suspected she was cheating. The user was at a party where the ex-girlfriend was rumored to have danced and kissed another guy. The user wasn't close to the ex and didn't see her at the party because it was a big venue with different friend circles.

When the user started dating the guy, he was still really hurt about the breakup and was questioning why they broke up. The user felt bad seeing him so upset and wanted a fresh start. So, when he asked her if she saw his ex at the party, she lied and said she saw her with other guys. This made him feel better, he moved on faster, and now he's happier without any regrets about his ex.

The user is wondering if lying in this situation makes them the asshole.

Okay, so to evaluate whether this action is morally acceptable, I need to consider a few things: the intent behind the lie, the consequences of the lie, and whether the lie was justified.

The intent here was to help the boyfriend feel better and move on from his ex. The user was motivated by a desire to make him happy and to have a healthy relationship without the baggage of his past. That seems like a good intention.

The consequences of the lie were that the boyfriend was able to move on faster and is now happier. He feels better knowing that his ex cheated, which he believes justified the breakup. So, in this case, the lie had a positive outcome for the boyfriend.

However, lying itself is generally considered morally wrong because it breaks trust. Trust is a fundamental component of any relationship, and lying can damage that trust, even if the intention was to protect someone's feelings.

But in this specific case, the lie didn't cause any harm beyond the initial deception. The boyfriend is happier now, and there's no indication that the lie will come back to haunt them or cause future problems. The user also mentions that there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now, which suggests that the lie wasn't motivated by personal gain but by a desire to help.

Another angle to consider is the concept of "benevolent lies." Sometimes, people lie to protect others from unnecessary pain or to help them in a difficult situation. In this case, the lie seems to have served that purpose by helping the boyfriend move on and feel better about the breakup.

On the other hand, some might argue that lying, even with good intentions, can set a precedent for future behavior. If the user continues to lie to protect their partner's feelings, it could lead to more significant issues down the line where the truth is necessary for the relationship's health.

But in this particular instance, the lie seems to have had a positive outcome without any negative consequences. The user didn't gain anything from the lie, and the boyfriend is better off because of it.

So, weighing the intent, the consequences, and the nature of the lie, it seems that while lying is generally not morally acceptable, in this specific case, the action can be seen as morally acceptable because it led to a positive outcome without causing harm.

Therefore, the answer would be that the action is morally acceptable.
